reader.decision: Approve the price.changed subscriber in every shop-api pod. Do not lower the CDN TTL. Before merging, confirm where start_invalidation() gets called, since shop/app.py was not found.
reader.decision_reason: The message says the stale price comes from the per-pod price_cache, not the CDN, and the CDN rule for /api/* has cache: false. So the CDN TTL change would do nothing. The subscriber reuses the existing price.changed event and removes the cause, at the cost of one Redis subscription per pod.

reconstruction.problem: After a price change in the admin, only the pod that handled the POST (pod A) clears its price_cache entry. The other 5 shop-api pods keep the old price in their per-process TTLCache with ttl=3600. price.changed is published, but only search/indexer.py subscribes. No shop-api pod listens.
reconstruction.what_breaks: Customers get mixed prices on reload, depending on which pod serves /api/prices. They can see the old price, including at checkout, for up to an hour. In the example, KET-2210 changed from 39.90 to 34.90 at 10:02 and the last old price appeared at 10:57. The CDN is not involved, because the /api/* rule has cache: false.
reconstruction.fix: Add start_invalidation() in pricing/service.py. It subscribes to price.changed and pops the SKU from price_cache. Call it at startup in shop/app.py. Keep the local pop in admin/prices.py. Make no change to cdn/rules.yaml. Other pods drop the entry in about 0.5 s (the sleep_time in shared/events.py), and customers see the new price within about a second.
reconstruction.cost: One Redis subscription per pod. A pod that misses a message while Redis is down keeps the old price until its TTL expires. The startup file shop/app.py was not found in the repository, so the exact place for the call is unconfirmed.

follow_up_questions: Where is the shop.app:app entrypoint actually defined, since shop/app.py was not found? The startup call must go in the right place.
Does subscribe() in shared/events.py run its handler in a background thread or loop in each pod, and is it safe to call price_cache.pop from there?
reader.closing_answer: Yes, I approve the price.changed subscriber in every shop-api pod, not the 60-second price_cache TTL. The TTL cut still leaves mixed prices for up to a minute. First locate the real startup module for shop.app:app so the start_invalidation() call goes in the right place.
